title: Analysis of NBD-lipid uptake in HeLa-CDC50A cells by Flow Cytometry
author: Klara KTS Scholtissek

steps.title: Maintain samples on cooling block
steps.instruction: Keep all cell samples on a cooling block throughout the flow cytometry analysis; measure technical duplicates sequentially and later average the results.

steps.title: Configure flow cytometer
steps.instruction: Set up the NovoCyte Quanteon 4025 flow cytometer (Agilent) with four lasers (405 nm, 488 nm, 561 nm, 637 nm) and 25 fluorescence detectors, running NovoExpress software v. 1.6.2.

substeps.instruction: BFP detection: 405 nm laser (Violet) with filter V445, laser gain set to 500.
NBD detection: 488 nm laser (Blue) with filter B530.
mCherry detection: 561 nm laser (Yellow‑Green) with filter Y615.
DRAQ7 detection: 637 nm laser (Red) with filter R695.

steps.title: Acquire data and exclude dead cells
steps.instruction: Run each sample, exclude dead cells using DRAQ7 staining, and collect between 2,000 and 10,000 events within the mCherry‑positive (or respective expression‑positive) quadrant gate.

steps.title: Apply gating hierarchy
steps.instruction: In FlowJo, redraw the following gates in order:

substeps.instruction: FSC vs SSC: draw a cell gate to exclude debris in the bottom‑left corner.
FSC‑A vs FSC‑H: draw a singlet gate (below a 45° line) to exclude doublets.
SSC‑A vs DRAQ7‑A: draw a live‑cell gate to exclude DRAQ7‑positive cells.
NBD‑A positive gate, mCherry‑A positive gate, or appropriate quadrant gates for the experimental read‑out.

steps.title: Export data for analysis
steps.instruction: Export the .fcs files of all samples and import them into FlowJo for further analysis.

steps.title: Normalize fluorescence expression
steps.instruction: For each population, calculate normalized expression by dividing the median NBD‑A intensity by the median mCherry‑A intensity; alternatively, divide median BFP‑A by median mCherry‑A if BFP is used.

steps.title: Export statistical summary
steps.instruction: Export a CSV file from FlowJo containing the statistics, including the median values of NBD‑A, mCherry‑A, and BFP‑A for each sample.
